subject: model vs. QTL significance in stepwiseqtl()

messages.author: 78954c94ee92247d
messages.subject: model vs. QTL significance in stepwiseqtl()
parts:
Karl,

Many thanks for your attention to this group. Your posts and those of others have been invaluable to me. 

I have a colleague who is a statistical geneticist and a computational biologist by training and he didn't think any additional QTL found by stepwise selection would be very significant, suggesting that perhaps these QTL are only significant when they are additive, i.e. the model as a whole is significant, but individually, the QTL may not be, in which case reporting them as QTL is misleading. I am wondering if it is worth reporting these stepwise models over/in addition to the QTL identified using scanone?  

I also see more QTL added by stepwiseqtl() when I use a denser marker coverage (7 markers/cM) but they drop out when I use a subset of that genotype data (1 marker/cM), which further reduces my confidence in the biological reality of QTL identified using this function. Do you have any thoughts on this? 

Regards
JC

parts: > I have a colleague who is a statistical geneticist and a computational biologist by training and he didn't think any additional QTL found by stepwise selection would be very significant, suggesting that perhaps these QTL are only significant when they are additive, i.e. the model as a whole is significant, but individually, the QTL may not be, in which case reporting them as QTL is misleading. I am wondering if it is worth reporting these stepwise models over/in addition to the QTL identified using scanone?

I don't understand the concern. I would report loci that I believe affect the phenotype. The consideration of multiple-QTL models can lead to the identification of additional loci, but this is not necessarily true.

> I also see more QTL added by stepwiseqtl() when I use a denser marker coverage (7 markers/cM) but they drop out when I use a subset of that genotype data (1 marker/cM), which further reduces my confidence in the biological reality of QTL identified using this function. Do you have any thoughts on this?

A detailed study of the relationship between the genotype at these loci and the phenotype may help to distinguish between artifacts and real effects.

karl

messages.author: d5fdb09d679f8c32
messages.subject: Re: model vs. QTL significance in stepwiseqtl()
parts: I have a colleague who is a statistical geneticist and a computational biologist by training and he didn't think any additional QTL found by stepwise selection would be very significant, suggesting that perhaps these QTL are only significant when they are additive, i.e. the model as a whole is significant, but individually, the QTL may not be, in which case reporting them as QTL is misleading. I am wondering if it is worth reporting these stepwise models over/in addition to the QTL identified using scanone?

The logic seems circular here.  If one thinks that only QTL that are individually significant are worth reporting, then those found from multiple QTL modeling using stepwiseqtl() are not worth it.

The reasons for considering QTL from multiple QTL modeling (detailed in the literature) include:
(1) reducing background variation from strong or moderate QTL
(2) detecting QTLs that interact (epistasis)
(3) accurately localizing linked QTL (to avoid ghost QTL)

That said, multiple QTL modeling is more involved, and there are some risks there.  So, one should examine the QTLs found carefully and convince oneself that they are not the result of any artifacts in the data.  One problem I have encountered a few times is outliers in the phenotype.  These may lead one to conclude that there are more QTL than the data really support.

I also see more QTL added by stepwiseqtl() when I use a denser marker coverage (7 markers/cM) but they drop out when I use a subset of that genotype data (1 marker/cM), which further reduces my confidence in the biological reality of QTL identified using this function. Do you have any thoughts on this?

Denser markers are more informative, so from that point of view one should find more QTL with the denser set.  That said, the informativeness of 7 markers per cM should not be very different from 1 marker per cM unless you have RI lines (in which case it would be somewhat different).  You may want to redo the stepwise with a lower threshold (maybe some QTL missed the threshold by a whisker).  You should also check for outliers in the phenotype.

Cheers,
Saunak
